prompt: Light travelling inside a glass optical fibre stays trapped and travels along the fibre, even around gentle bends. This works when light inside the glass:

options.text: Hits the glass surface at a very shallow, grazing angle and speeds up out of the fibre
Is absorbed and re-emitted by atoms along the fibre
Hits the boundary at an angle greater than the critical angle, so it reflects entirely back inside
Changes into an electrical signal at each bend

explanation: In total internal reflection, light in a denser medium striking the boundary at more than the critical angle cannot refract out and is reflected completely back inside, which is how optical fibres guide light.
